# Teaching guide {.unnumbered}

This page is for whoever leads the sessions. It suggests a schedule for the
RNA-seq module, what to prepare, and where learners usually get stuck.

## Format

Five sessions of about 90 minutes work well: roughly a third of each session
spent explaining, two thirds hands-on. Learners need a laptop (macOS, Linux,
or Windows with WSL) where the [practice setup](rna-seq/practice-setup.qmd) is
already done; ask them to do it **before** session 1, and hold a short
drop-in for anyone stuck. Session 5's pipeline run needs a SLURM cluster
account. Sessions 1 and 2 are the slowest for true
beginners; don't rush them, because every later session depends on being
comfortable in the shell.

| Session | Chapters | Hands-on goal |
|---|---|---|
| 1. From the sequencer to the shell | [After submission](rna-seq/after-submission.qmd), [Computing](rna-seq/computing.qmd), [Shell basics](rna-seq/shell-basics.qmd) | Open a terminal, `source env.sh`, find the practice FASTQs, `zcat \| head`, count reads, redirect output to a file |
| 2. Opening every file | [Sequence files](rna-seq/sequence-files.qmd), [Annotation files](rna-seq/annotation-files.qmd), [Alignment files](rna-seq/alignment-files.qmd) | Decode a FASTQ header and quality; count gene types in the GTF; make a BED of genes; decode SAM flags |
| 3. Cleaning and checking reads | [Tools landscape](rna-seq/tools-landscape.qmd), [Pipeline map](rna-seq/pipeline-map.qmd), [FastQC](rna-seq/fastqc.qmd), [Trimming](rna-seq/trimming.qmd) | Run FastQC and Trim Galore on the practice data; compare read counts before and after |
| 4. Where did the reads come from? | [Salmon](rna-seq/salmon.qmd), [Alignment](rna-seq/alignment.qmd), [Signal tracks](rna-seq/signal-tracks.qmd), [Merging](rna-seq/merging.qmd), [MultiQC](rna-seq/multiqc.qmd), [tximport](rna-seq/tximport.qmd) | Run Salmon, HISAT2 and bamCoverage on all four samples; IGV; MultiQC; tximport in R |
| 5. The whole pipeline, and R | [Snakemake](rna-seq/snakemake.qmd), [Running the pipeline](rna-seq/running-rnapipe.qmd), [Into R](rna-seq/into-r.qmd), [TT-seq](rna-seq/tt-seq.qmd) | Launch `RNApipe` on the practice data **at the start** (cluster users), then DESeq2 on the session 4 outputs while it runs |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start the pipeline run early

The practice data finish in well under an hour, but queue times vary. Have
learners launch `sbatch RNApipe.sh` at the **start** of session 5 and work on
DESeq2 while it runs. Without a cluster, skip the launch: the step chapters
already did every step by hand.
:::

## Before the first session

- [ ] Every learner has finished the [practice setup](rna-seq/practice-setup.qmd):
      `conda activate rnaseq-tools` works and `ls $DATA` shows eight FASTQ files.
- [ ] Decide on references: `chr22` (fast, laptop-friendly) or `full`. Building
      full references during a session takes too long: build them beforehand,
      once, somewhere shared if you can.
- [ ] Everyone has IGV installed (desktop version), or uses
      [igv.org/app](https://igv.org/app) in the browser.
- [ ] For session 5: cluster accounts work, and bagPipes' config has a reference
      block filled in. In the current bagPipes `main`, **every reference line is
      commented out** ([Running the pipeline](rna-seq/running-rnapipe.qmd#choose-the-reference)).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## On UNC Longleaf (Phanstiel lab)

Learners can skip building references and use the prebuilt ones in
`/proj/phanstiel_lab/Reference/human/hg38/` (see Practice setup), and run the
hands-on boxes inside `srun -p interact ...` jobs with `module load` instead of
conda. Check everyone can `ssh` in and read `/proj/phanstiel_lab` beforehand.
:::

## Where people get stuck

| Sticking point | What helps |
|---|---|
| "Where am I?" in the terminal | Ask them to run `pwd` before every command for the first session |
| Forgetting `source $WALK/env.sh` / `conda activate` in a new terminal | Put both on the board at the start of every session |
| Running heavy commands on a cluster login node | Show `srun --pty` (interactive job) early, in session 1 |
| Apple Silicon conda errors | `CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64` ([Where to run](rna-seq/computing.qmd#getting-the-software-conda)) |
| Tabs vs spaces in the samplesheet | Open it with `cat -A` so tabs show as `^I` |
| Thinking TPM and counts are interchangeable | Draw a long and a short gene with the same number of reads |
| Strand-specific tracks look "backwards" | Go over the dUTP explanation in [Signal tracks](rna-seq/signal-tracks.qmd#which-strand-is-which) |
| Snakemake lock after a cancelled job | `./unlock.sh rna`, covered in [Running the pipeline](rna-seq/running-rnapipe.qmd) |

## Extending to other assays

The ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq / CUT&Tag / CUT&RUN modules will reuse the
Foundations part unchanged. In the repository, each assay gets its own folder
(`rna-seq/`, `atac-seq/`, `chip-seq/`) and its own `part:` in `_quarto.yml`.
